verdictStatement: The envelope6 schema stays byte-identical to subject01 and keeps its review01 conditional acceptance. correction02 disposes of review01 F1, F2, F4 and F5 as a reference correction. The review01 F3 premise was wrong and is withdrawn. J-INTERRUPTION-LEDGER agrees with the pinned owner model on all 46 generated ledgers (default, fit, audit-like, candidates; every cancel point and signal). It refuses shape-valid Run erasure, earlier-Run substitution, forged record terminations, phase/signal mismatch and after-settle reclassification. It still cannot select the prose and join: F-A (the override prose says 'no earlier committed Run', but the rule it adopts ignores optional-step Runs) and F-B (the join trusts invocation-record admission that no pinned owner implements) must be resolved first. F-C and F-D are recommended. The parent envelope5 remains an unaccepted report04 candidate, and report05/author05 corrections are independent. Nothing here implies report readiness.

preconditionChallenge.rootStatement: The join runs after complete invocation/step/DAG/Run and normal D9 admission, over trusted host custody. It is not authority for arbitrary records.
whatTheJoinActuallyRederives: correlation equality (requestId, projectId, clientCorrelationId presence and value)
contiguous stepId membership for steps and results
exact aggregate {interrupted, signal, runId of last required completed runId}
run-carrier equality with the step AnalysisResult
whatItAssumesButNoPinnedOwnerImplements: cancelled outcome <=> interrupted step termination with the cancellation signal
no completed/started step after a cancelled required dependency (the model cancels every step from cancelAt onward)
result kind bound to step kind (only analysis/verify yield AnalysisResult)
record custody (the record is the one this host wrote)
preconditionChallenge.assessment: Honest but under-specified. The pinned workflows_model.v1.py has a generator (run_invocation) and validate_dag, but no invocation-record admission function. The report04 J-LEDGER-CANCELLATION covers 'cancelled outcome <=> interrupted termination' only for report documents and is itself unaccepted. So 'prior normal admission' names a duty without a pinned owner implementation. That is acceptable for a reference trial, but prose selection must either name the prerequisite joins or fold the per-step checks into J-INTERRUPTION-LEDGER.

findings.title: Override prose says 'no earlier committed Run' but adopts the required-only D9 rule
findings.detail: The override after-text says the interruption form applies 'when this invocation has no earlier committed Run' and also 'derive the committed Run choice from the owned D9 ledger rule'. The pinned model (workflows_model.v1.py:376-382) and ledger_join.py consider only required steps. Cancellation owner text (workflows-and-surfaces.md:226) says 'a Run committed by an earlier step' without qualification. D5 shows an optional analysis step that durably committed a Run in this invocation, followed by a before-settle interrupt of a required step. The result is the empty failure form with no runId, which the join admits. The two override sentences disagree, and the owner rule versus owner text is ambiguous.
findings.required: The owner must decide whether an optional-step Run is named. Then either qualify the prose ('no committed Run from a required step, per the D9 ledger rule') or change the rule and join. Add a golden either way.

findings.title: The join's precondition is narrower than a true completed-ledger admission, and its prerequisite has no pinned owner
findings.detail: See preconditionChallenge. D4 admits a ledger with inconsistent per-step cancellation signals and a completed render after a cancelled dependency. D7b shows a query step carrying an AnalysisResult is shape-valid and would count as a commit. D10 shows malformed input escapes untyped. The join's own safety properties (erasure, substitution) depend on these unpinned admissions.
findings.required: Name the prerequisite joins (per-step cancelled<=>interrupted with the same signal, the cancellation suffix law, the result-kind/step-kind binding) as host duties beside J-INTERRUPTION-LEDGER, or fold them in. Refusals must be typed.

findings.title: The no-commit branch does not police the carrier, so the contract's 'no invented detail / no fabricated completion' is unenforced
findings.detail: D6: with no committed Run, the join admits an interrupted kind=failure with an unrelated nonempty DomainDetail, a kind=query carrying a queryRecord for a cancelled query, and a kind=invocation carrying a different record. The root defers nonempty errors to the existing observation/detail owner. But an interrupted aggregate has no route detail for native §10 composition to supply, and D9 says DomainDetailCode never names a termination, so no existing owner check is identified. Invocation-record equality is enforced only when a Run was committed.
findings.required: Before settle with no commit, restrict the carrier to the new empty failure form, an invocation carrier equal to the record, or a named existing owner form (such as doctor). Or name the owner check that refuses invented details and completions. Apply invocation equality in both branches.

findings.title: Interruption before planning or record admission has no join path
findings.detail: invocation:3 orderedSteps has minItems 1, and the override makes J-INTERRUPTION-LEDGER mandatory before selecting the form. A signal during argument parsing, startup or plan admission has no admitted record, so the duty is unsatisfiable exactly where 'pre-Run' is most literal. Also, report04's ledger law admits unrecorded required steps (render), while the join requires a result for every step (J-INTERRUPTION-STEPS). No pinned owner text states when the invocation record comes into existence relative to signal handling.
findings.required: The owner must state the pre-record case: either no signal is honoured before record admission, or the form is selectable under a declared no-record precondition. Reconcile unrecorded steps with the report ledger when rebasing.
